newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish shares end at new record ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: Finnish shares end at new record ahead of holiday.

text.p: Shares set their fourth consecutive record on Thursday and closed at the new peak for Finland's Independence Day holiday as the market remained bullish, brokers said.
The HEX's new record stood 2471.14 points after the index advanced 0.49 percent in relatively strong 430 million markka volume.

Brokers saw some risk of a downward correction next week but low bond yields continued to lend support altghough the long end of the curve rose nine basis points in disappointment that Germany's Bundesbank did not trim its repo rate.
Telecommunications group Nokia closed 2.20 markka higher at 266.00 as the dollar remained quite strong and the greenback also helped forestry stocks hold gains from earlier in the week.
The forestry index was up 0.12 percent with UPM-Kymmene flat and Metsa-Serla B up 0.50 at 33.00 markka. Enso was also flat.

Pharmaceuticals group Orion rose to 163.00 markka -- its highest since June 19 -- and closed up 3.50 markka at 161.00 as the sector received attention amid rumours that investment company Investor would have sold its stake in Swedish Astra.

Finvest added 0.30 to 5.60 in lively trade on positive recommendations from analysts and brokers said there were hopes that Nokia's recovery would help electronics components makers like Finvest and Aspo, which rose 8.10 markka or over four percent to close at a new 193.00 record.
